key_insight: DFT predicts stronger vacancy association in CrN than TiN, with compact mixed-vacancy clusters remaining stabilised at CrN(001) surfaces but becoming unfavourable at TiN(001) surfaces.
engineering_relevance: Accounting for nitrogen availability and vacancy depth could help guide defect control in TiN and CrN coatings.
method: DFT calculations of native vacancies in bulk rocksalt TiN and CrN and at (001) surfaces.
Formation energies evaluated across phase-stability-constrained chemical potentials.
Association energies referenced to isolated vacancies, using preferred depths for surface comparisons.
evidence_signal: For compact clusters containing two metal and two nitrogen vacancies, association energies change from +0.217 to −0.346 eV per vacancy in TiN and from +1.188 to +0.431 eV per vacancy in CrN between bulk and surface; positive values indicate favourable association.
watch_item: The abstract reports DFT energetics, not experimental validation or vacancy migration kinetics, so practical clustering rates remain unresolved.
paper_title: Native vacancy energetics and association in TiN and CrN: chemical potential dependence, clustering, and surface effects
